question: A sum of money **doubles itself in 5 years** at **simple interest**. In how many years will it become **four times** itself?

lines.say: A sum of money doubles in 5 years at simple interest.
So it becomes four times in 10 years. Right?
Wrong. 10 years is the trap, and most students fall for it.
Here is the question. A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become four times itself?
Is it 10 years, 15 years, 20 years, or 12 years?
Pause the video, and pick your option.
Step one. Take 100 rupees. Doubling means it becomes 200 rupees in 5 years.
So the interest for 5 years is 100 rupees.
Step two. Simple interest is always on the original 100. So every 5 years, you earn the same 100 rupees again.

card.title: Step 2 · Simple interest is flat
rows: Interest is on the original ₹100 only

lines.say: Step three. Four times means 400 rupees. That is 300 rupees of interest.
100 rupees every 5 years. So 300 takes three blocks of 5 years. 15 years.
In 10 years, the money is only three times.
The shortcut. Under simple interest, count the interest, not the multiple.

rows: Doubles in T years → n times in **(n − 1) × T** years

lines.say: Four times. 4 minus 1 is 3. 3 times 5 is 15 years.
